new_groups.label: From the Archduke Charles's headquarters, 27 October 1796: Moreau's army retreats across the Rhine
new_groups.definition: Printings of a letter dated at the headquarters of the Archduke Charles of Austria, 27 October 1796, which the London Gazette of 13 November published with others from Captain Anstruther and R. Crauford: 'My Lord, I have the honour to inform your Lordship, that in the course of the last night Gen. Moreau's army retreated across the Rhine at Huningen' (the Patowmac Guardian's words); it is signed Robert Crauford. Three papers print it after a London paragraph of 14 November that introduces it as 'the last of the letters alluded to'; the New Hampshire Gazette prints the letter alone, from New York. The writer's report from the Austrian headquarters, as the London Gazette published it.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Truguet to the Directory, 6 November 1796: letters from Brest 'announce that a general revolution has just taken place in Ireland'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a letter to the French Executive Directory dated 6 November 1796 and signed Truguet: 'I hasten to communicate to the Executive Directory the reception of letters from Brest, of the 3d instant (November) brought by an extraordinary courier, which announce that a general revolution has just taken place in Ireland.' It gives the report of the captains of two ships brought in from Liverpool by French privateers, that the Irish had taken 30,000 stand of arms in Dublin and defeated 10,000 English troops. Printed from the Paris papers, in the same column of French news as General Bournonville's letter (a group of its own). A report at second hand: the writer passes on what letters from Brest and two ship captains said.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: General Bournonville to the Directory, Mulheim, 3 Brumaire: the attack on the bridgehead at Neuwied
new_groups.definition: Printings of General Bournonville's letter to the French Executive Directory from Mulheim, dated 3 Brumaire (two papers add 'Oct. 28'): 'I had the honor to give you an account yesterday of the attack of the army made by the enemy in the night between the 29th and 30th Vendemiaire ... upon the head of the bridge and the isle of Neuwied'; he writes that the enemy meant to make the garrison prisoners of war, and that 'This affair cost the enemy more than four thousand men'. Printed from the Paris papers, in the same column as Truguet's letter of 6 November (a group of its own). A commander's own report.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: General Berthier's letter from Milan, 28 November 1796: the army of Italy after Arcola
new_groups.definition: Printings of a letter from General Berthier, chief of the staff of the army of Italy, to General Baraguey d'Hilliers (each paper spells the name differently), dated at Milan, 8 Frimaire, 28 November 1796: 'I informed you, general, by the last bulletin which I sent you, that, after having beaten the troops commanded by general Alvinzy in person, at Arcola, the commander in chief made his dispositions to attack the column commanded by general Davidovich'; it reports that the enemy was driven from the heights of Rivoli with 1,100 prisoners taken. A staff officer's own report for the French side.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Delarue's report to the Council of Five Hundred on the march of the troops, August 1797
new_groups.definition: Printings of the report made in the French Council of Five Hundred (sitting of 4 August 1797; 3 August in the Mirror) by Delarue ('Delarne' in the Mirror and the Kentucky Gazette) for its committee of inspectors, 'on the march of the troops': 'It results from the information we have procured, 1. That from 26 to 27,000 men have been detached from the army of the Sambre and Meuse, instead of 9000, as was stated by Gen. Hoche. 2. That this force directed its march towards Paris' (the Gazette of the United States prints 6000, 'as was said'). It goes on to say that the soldiers had been 'misled and seduced' against the Legislative Body and that troops kept marching on Paris 'by order of Gen. Hoche'. A committee's report and charges in the legislature, as the Paris papers gave them.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Vienna, 26 July 1797: the peace talks in Italy 'meet with great difficulties'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a report from Vienna dated 26 July 1797, printed from the London papers in two forms. Three papers print a short form: 'The Marquis DE GALLO, has this moment arrived here from Udina. The negotiations for peace in Italy, meet with great difficulties. The French require that Mantua shall be united with the Cisalpine Republic' (the Mirror's words). The Gazette of the United States and the Kentucky Gazette print a longer form that opens with the Marquis de Gallo's conferences with the Emperor and Baron Thugut, and adds that 'neither the marquis nor the persons about the court had very pleasant countenances'. Both forms then give the same account of the French demand for Mantua, the Emperor's indemnification in Istria and Dalmatia, and 'our fears that hostilities may again commence'. A correspondent's report, at second hand through the London papers.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Wilmington, 12 October 1797: a traveller from Pensacola reports orders to deliver up the Spanish posts
new_groups.definition: Printings of a report from Wilmington, North Carolina, of 12 October 1797: 'A gentleman who arrived in town on Sunday last from New-Providence, via the Havannah, has favored the Printer with the following information—on the authenticity of which he places the greatest confidence': on 20 August, the day he left Pensacola, he saw an official letter from the Baron de Carondelet saying that orders had come from his court 'to put into full execution, the treaty between Spain and the United States of America', and that the commandants of the forts on the Mississippi were to deliver up the posts; Governor Gayoso had been appointed governor-general of the Floridas and Louisiana. A traveller's report at second hand.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: A letter from Nassau, New Providence, 26 September 1797: the writer's account of a 'plot'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a letter from a gentleman at Nassau, New Providence, dated 26 September 1797, as a Columbia (South Carolina) paper printed it on 3 November: 'We have lately very providentially escaped a most hellish plot.—A parcel of French negroes who had been captured and sold here, and who had ran away from their owners, entered into a conspiracy (about thirty in number) to burn the town and make a general massacre of the whites.' By his account one of them told his master a few hours before, five were taken and condemned and three executed. One correspondent's account, written from the side of those who held the accused; the accused are heard only through it, and it names no one.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

dispositions_summary.method: The automatic families first printed in 1797 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 240 items printed somewhere; by the finder's count 3 reach 5 papers, 29 reach 4, 140 reach 3). The same script was run with year 1796 over the 1797 pages (items_from_1796.json: 49 items, 13 in 4 papers, all parts of one publication of January). Every item in 4 or more papers was read, the items in 2 or 3 papers were checked automatically for a further paper by a wider text match, and the counts were checked item by item with phrase searches over all 1,587 pages of 1797 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json); every hit was read. AI review on the session's own model; not an independent human review.
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: Adopted for 1797 on 23 November 2026, on the review's recommendation, which the owner asked it to follow: a story needs one single printed item in 4 or more papers, because only 8 series survive for 1797 (three all year, 2 to 6 in print in any three weeks), so no item reaches 7 papers, or 6; 1793 uses 6 for the same reason. Every single item in 5 papers was admitted, except digests; items in 4 papers were chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news: every document, letter or report in 4 papers was chosen, and single paragraphs of London, Paris and Hamburg news columns, verse, an anecdote and a printer's notice were not. Items are counted by their own words; a printing counts where its opening survives; two printed forms of one report are counted together, as 1809 counted two translations of one bulletin. A sub-story could have fewer papers under a parent that reaches the threshold; this round has none. The 21 stories of rounds one and two stay as they are; this round adds groups beside them.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted item by item, two single items of 1797 reach 5 papers: the Tenerife report (a story of round one) and the Vienna report of 26 July (in two printed forms, 3 + 2 papers). Twenty-five reach 4: the eight stories admitted here; seven stories of rounds one and two (Adams's farewell address, the paragraph on Andrew Brown's death, Blount's letter, the Algerine battle, the brig Brothers, the Hermione 'Particulars' and Duncan's Camperdown dispatch); and ten items read and not admitted (below). Everything else read is in 3 papers or fewer.
counted_item_by_item.Joins made by the finder: The finder joins items that were printed together in one run of news. The run of Paris news of early November 1796 that four papers printed (Gazette of the United States 9 January, Patowmac Guardian 19 January, Republican Gazetteer 24 January, Kentucky Gazette 8 March) holds Truguet's letter, Bournonville's letter and the Paris paragraph on the Dey of Algiers, each in those 4 papers, and other paragraphs in 1 to 3. The London news of late August 1797 joins the Brussels paragraph on the definitive treaty and the paragraph on dispatches from Scotland, each in 4 papers. Each was counted by its own words.
counted_item_by_item.Openings that do not survive: The President's message of 19 January 1797 with the Secretary of State's letter to Mr. Pinckney was printed in instalments. Its opening survives in 3 papers (Gazette of the United States, New Hampshire Gazette, Patowmac Guardian); the Virginia Argus of 14 February and the Republican Gazetteer of 28 February hold only its continuation, their earlier issues being lost. By the rule other years used (a printing counts where its opening survives; 1809 dropped such a page), it is in 3 papers.
counted_item_by_item.Pages that only quote an item: Not counted: the Gazette of the United States of 5 June, which quotes Adams's speech of 16 May; the Secretary of State's letter to the Spanish minister of 8 August, which quotes the 'western letter' on the Spanish posts; a New Hampshire Gazette digest of 22 November that rewords the Hague paragraph of 19 September.
counted_item_by_item.A printing missed by round two: Adams's reply of 29 November 1797 to the House of Representatives is also on page 2 of the New Hampshire Gazette of 13 December; that issue's RevX transcriptions are filed one page off, so round two's phrase searches missed it. With it the reply is in 4 papers. Decided 23 November 2026 to add it; deferred to a correction release (see deferred_addition).

stories_of_rounds_one_and_two.reach the 1797 threshold (4 papers by on: Eight: the Tenerife report (5), Duncan's Camperdown dispatches (4), the Algerine-Sicilian battle (4), the Hermione 'Particulars' (4), the brig Brothers (4), Adams's farewell address (4), Blount's letter (4), and the paragraph on Andrew Brown's death (4). A ninth, Adams's reply to the House of November 1797, reaches 4 once the deferred printing is added.
stories_of_rounds_one_and_two.kept below the threshold: Thirteen as admitted (twelve once the deferred printing is added), kept as reviewed stories though no item of theirs reaches 4 papers: the opening of Congress of November 1797 (3 per item until then), Boyd / Bantry coverage (3), Barney escapes the blockade (3), Sonthonax leaves Saint-Domingue (3), Quito earthquake (3), Peace / Cayenne context (2), Peace and Plenty boarding (3), Two Sisters wreck (two texts, 1 paper each), French captures at Havana (3), Special session of Congress (3 per item, 5 papers across its parts), Kosciuszko's land warrant (3), Jefferson's letter to Madison (3), New Hampshire governor's address (3). Decided 23 November 2026 (the owner asked the review to follow its recommendations): kept, because they were read and checked against their scans before the rule, the Boyd story is the pilot that the release's consumer view and checks are built on, and treating them as not admitted would need a correction release and changes to the site for no gain in accuracy. Recorded as an exception for the full audit (docs/rules-and-exceptions.md).
